coords: normalised 0-1, origin top-left of the frame
note: explode.frames[j].anchors are the 2D anchor points of each labelled part in explode frame j; labels are meant to be shown on the last (fully exploded) frame. rotate anchors are informational (visible=false means occluded at that angle).

parts.name: CPU Socket (AM4)
parts.description: The 1331-hole AM4 socket that holds a Ryzen processor; the lever clamps the CPU's pins in place.

parts.name: VRM Heatsink
parts.description: An aluminium block over the CPU's power stages that soaks up their heat so the voltage stays clean under load.

parts.name: Chipset (B550)
parts.description: AMD's B550 hub chip: it runs the extra USB, SATA and PCIe lanes and links them to the CPU.

parts.name: RAM Slots (DDR4 ×4)
parts.description: Four DDR4 DIMM slots in dual channel, for up to 128 GB of memory; the latches lock each stick in.

parts.name: PCIe x16 Slot
parts.description: The full-length slot wired straight to the CPU, where the graphics card plugs in (PCIe 4.0 x16).

parts.name: M.2 SSD Slots
parts.description: Two M.2 sockets for NVMe SSDs that lie flat on the board: one runs off the CPU, one off the chipset.

parts.name: 24-Pin ATX Power
parts.description: The main power input from the PSU, feeding 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V to the board, RAM and slots.

parts.name: 8-Pin CPU Power
parts.description: A dedicated 12 V input from the PSU that the VRM converts into the processor's core voltage.

parts.name: Rear I/O Ports
parts.description: The ports at the back of the case: USB, HDMI and DisplayPort, Gigabit LAN, Wi-Fi antennas and audio jacks.

parts.name: SATA Ports
parts.description: Four right-angle SATA 6 Gb/s connectors for 2.5" SSDs, hard drives and optical drives.

parts.name: CMOS Battery
parts.description: A CR2032 coin cell that keeps the BIOS settings and the real-time clock alive while the PC is unplugged.
